question: Should OpenClaw pursue distributed job orchestration as a core Gateway feature, a plugin-provided backend/API seam, or documented external orchestration while the narrower cron, session, and runtime trackers proceed separately?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the owner boundary, backend contract, config shape, failure semantics, observability surface, and dependency/security posture require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design Backend-Neutral Orchestration
options.body: Define shared scheduler/job ownership, worker claiming, retries, dead-letter, and observability contracts first, then decide whether Redis/BullMQ is one implementation behind that seam.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Tracks
options.body: Keep this issue as prior art while cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and plugin/API issues each own their narrower implementation choices.

options.title: Document External Orchestration
options.body: Decide not to add a core backend for now and document safe external queue or scheduler patterns around OpenClaw deployments.

recommendation.title: Design Backend-Neutral Orchestration
recommendation.body: Define shared scheduler/job ownership, worker claiming, retries, dead-letter, and observability contracts first, then decide whether Redis/BullMQ is one implementation behind that seam.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided keep-open architecture guidance and has the strongest feature-history signal across command queue, cron, and task scheduling surfaces.
